title: Virtual Reality Therapy to Improve Arthroplasty Outcomes
official: Pilot Randomised Controlled Trial of Virtual Reality Immersive Therapy (VRIT) in Addition to Usual Care Compared to Usual Care in Patients Undergoing Joint Arthroplasty - VROOM Trial
summary:
Virtual reality (VR) has recently emerged as a non-medication-based method to manage anxiety. The patient wears a VR headset and is offered an immersive environment with hypnotic components with sound and imagery in a 3D environment. VR creates an immersive 3D environment and diverts attention away from worrying thoughts (anxiety) and pain and has been found useful to manage minor procedural pain and related anxiety.

This is a pilot feasibility trial to evaluate the effectiveness of VR in improving patient related outcomes (PROM) after joint replacement surgery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* NHS Highland patients
* Able to provide written informed consent (remotely)
* ASA Grade 1 and 2
* Listed for elective surgery at NHSH NTC
* Adults\>18 years undergoing joint arthroplasty surgery (hip and knee) will be included
* Fluent in English
* Able to receive and write emails
* Willing to comply with study protocols/training
* Access to Wi-Fi to undertake VRIT and complete questionnaires online

Exclusion Criteria:

* Not able to provide written informed consent
* Considered unsuitable by Clinician (with reason)
* Vision /hearing difficulties which preclude interaction with immersive environment
* Unable or unwilling to comply with study procedures and activities
* Participation in another interventional trial which undermines the scientific basis of the study
* Have a history of alcohol or substance abuse or Parkinson's disease or Multiple Sclerosis or Labyrinthitis (Ménière's disease), history of seizures, motion sickness or dementia
* Non NHS Highland patients
* Photosensitive epilepsy
* Patients with surgery scheduled for a Friday
sponsor: NHS Highland Research, Development and Innovation Organisation
